case_title.reason: Matches the judgment's header title, with 'v.' and 'ETC.' as printed.

number_of_accused.reason: Only original accused No.1 (the appellant) is before the Court; the other accused were acquitted and not appealed.

accused_gender.reason: The appellant is referred to throughout with male pronouns ('he', 'his'), so Male is supported.

accused_age.reason: The judgment gives no age for the appellant; only the victim's age of 22 is stated.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated in the judgment.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: The appellant's occupation is not mentioned; only the victim's computer course is noted.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on the appellant's wealth, poverty or class appears in the judgment.

previous_criminal_record.reason: The judgment says nothing about any prior criminal record of the appellant.

victim_gender.reason: The victim Hitesh Thakur is referred to as 'his son' and with male pronouns; Male is supported.

victim_age.reason: The judgment expressly states the victim was 22 years of age.

victim_caste.reason: No caste or community of the victim is named in the judgment.

victim_religion.reason: No religious identity of the victim is stated in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: Friends at a drink party, with trial court noting cordial relations and no enmity, is supported by the judgment.

offence_category.reason: The Supreme Court held the offence to be culpable homicide not amounting to murder, so this category fits.

statutory_provisions.reason: Charged sections and the finally restored s.304 Part II conviction are both stated in the judgment.

weapon.reason: The judgment repeatedly identifies a knife as the weapon used.

evidence_type.reason: Eyewitnesses, knife recovery, injury nature and PW-2 corroboration of the call are all described in the judgment.

confession.reason: The judgment mentions no confession or admission by the appellant.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Six knife blows, knife use and victim being unarmed are noted, with the High Court's reliance and its non-decisiveness recorded.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: Sudden fight, no premeditation, offering water, hospital transport and staying until last rites are all noted.

trial_court_outcome.reason: Trial court convicted under s.304 Part II with five years RI, Rs.10,000 fine and one year default term.

high_court_outcome.reason: High Court upheld the factual finding, altered the conviction to s.302 with life and fine, and affirmed co-accused acquittals.

final_outcome.reason: Conviction was modified to s.304 Part II, which fits the conviction_modified category.

offence_finally_established.reason: The Supreme Court held the appellant guilty under s.304 Part II, culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

imprisonment_type.reason: A fixed term of rigorous imprisonment for 10 years was imposed.

imprisonment_years.reason: The Supreme Court sentenced the appellant to 10 years rigorous imprisonment.

fine_rs.reason: A fine of Rs.10,000 is imposed, as stated in the operative order.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Neutral summary of the incident and evidence without reference to the later separation of co-accused
neutral_facts.quote: three of them were later separated from the case
neutral_facts.reason: Refers to later separation of three co-accused, which hints at court outcome; the summary should not reveal proceedings or outcomes.

offence_severity.reason: The judgment gives only a respondents' submission about life imprisonment, not a statutory prescription, so Not stated fits.

attempt_completion.reason: The victim was killed, so the offence was completed.

physical_harm.reason: Six knife wounds on different parts of the body, with the victim dying, are stated.

number_of_offences.reason: Two sections charged (s.302; s.201 r/w s.34) and one conviction (s.304 Part II) standing is supported.

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is involved in the case.

premeditation_planning.reason: The Court found the assault was sudden, without premeditation, and in heat of passion.

motive.correct_value: Sudden quarrel after victim, while smoking, blew smoke on accused's face (accepted as trigger); trial court found no proven motive
motive.quote: while smoking, blew smoke on the face of the appellant
motive.reason: The judgment says 'smoking', not 'cigarette'; the word 'cigarette' is an added detail.

key_evidence_accepted.reason: Eyewitness testimony, knife recovery, injury attribution and PW-2 corroboration are relied on by the Court.

witness_credibility.reason: The Court upheld concurrent findings on PW-11 and PW-12, eyewitnesses present throughout, and PW-2's corroboration.

post_offence_conduct.reason: Offering water, taking the victim to hospital, staying, and calling the father are all noted by the Court.

custody_duration.reason: The appellant's counsel stated the custody period and remission, as recorded in the judgment.

bail_history.reason: The judgment does not mention any bail grant or refusal.

trial_duration.reason: All listed dates (offence, trial judgment, High Court and Supreme Court) match the judgment.

legal_representation.reason: Counsel for the appellant and the respondents match the appearance list in the judgment.

investigation_status.correct_value: Statement under s.154 CrPC recorded; investigation proceeded; four accused sent for trial
investigation_status.quote: investigation proceeded, four accused ... were sent for trial
investigation_status.reason: The judgment does not say 'FIR' or that investigation was 'completed'; these are inferred.

procedural_irregularity.reason: The Court notes no procedural lapse by the courts below.

appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court modification to s.302 and Supreme Court partial allowance with s.304 Part II and 10 years match the judgment.

prosecution_argument.reason: Respondents argued the evidence supports guilt, the High Court's murder finding was justified, and the appeals lacked merit.

defence_argument.reason: Contradictions, doubtful genesis, Exception 4 alternative, and sentence already undergone match the appellant's submissions.

legal_principle_applied.reason: Exception 4 to s.300 and the overall-view approach, with wounds and knife use not decisive, are the Court's stated test.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: Surain Singh v. State of Punjab (2017) 5 SCC 796 is the only precedent relied on, with its citation given.

sentencing_rationale.reason: The Court notes no special reasons were recorded for the light sentence and explains why 10 years meets the ends of justice.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Sudden fight, heat of passion, no premeditation, no undue advantage and no intention to cause death are weighed by the Court.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The Court cites the nature of offence, trivial reason for anger, knife use and multiple blows as not warranting light punishment.

other_sentence_order.reason: The Court directs set-off under s.428 CrPC, which is the only other order in the judgment.
